task: TD-entry dispatcher semantics for claimed approval continuations
decision: Once a TD topic run has been claimed for dispatch, resume detection must not rely on `scheduler_state == 'resume_queued'` because the claim repo mutates queued rows to `claimed` before returning them. The dispatcher should treat any claimed topic run with a preserved `continuation_payload_json` as a resume continuation, reuse the paused `pipeline_task_id` when it still exists in the task store, and pass the stored resume payload/approval data through to `run_td_content_production_task()`.
rationale: Live manual QA showed approved TD cards restarting from `Building brief ...` and later 409ing on stale brief-approval task ids. The durable topic run still held a `resume_stage='brief_approval'` continuation payload, but the dispatcher discarded it because the claim snapshot no longer said `resume_queued` after the DB claim step. Resume semantics in this architecture belong to the durable continuation payload, not to the transient post-claim scheduler string.
alternatives: Continue keying resume detection off `scheduler_state == 'resume_queued'` — rejected because claimed rows no longer have that state by the time the dispatcher sees them

Change the repo to return pre-claim state strings in the snapshot — possible, but rejected for this fix because the continuation payload already provides the stable signal and keeps the change smaller
Always create a fresh task for every resume — rejected because it restarts TD pipelines from the top and invalidates frontend HITL task ids
outcome: Implemented on 2026-04-10. Claimed TD resume rows are now detected via non-empty continuation payloads, paused task ids are reused, and the stored `td_resume_payload` / `td_resume_approval` flow back into `run_td_content_production_task()`. Validation: `venv/bin/pytest tests/api/test_content_v13_ga_endpoints.py -k 'resume_claim_reuses_existing_task_id' -q` (1 passed), `venv/bin/pytest tests/api/test_content_v13_ga_endpoints.py -q` (33 passed, 2 pre-existing warnings), `venv/bin/pytest tests/api/test_content_v13.py -q` (75 passed, 13 pre-existing warnings), `venv/bin/pytest tests/content_engine/test_topic_run_service.py -q` (6 passed).

task: TD-entry start-production semantics under shared CE semaphore pressure
decision: TD start-production should expose an explicit queue state before actual CE execution begins. The HTTP route now preflights Redis GA-card state for the requested `topic_assignment_id`s and rejects duplicates with 409 when the same topic is already `content_queued` or `briefing` for the same `ga_run_id`. On first acceptance it persists a visible `content_queued` state to GA Redis cards and durable topic runs, and the frontend reflects that queue state instead of optimistically switching the card to `briefing`. The durable `briefing` transition remains runner-owned after `task_store.pipeline_semaphore(task_id)` acquires capacity.
rationale: The Webflow WE-177 test run proved that the old contract was lying to the user: a 202 response plus frontend optimistic `briefing` made a card look active even while the task was still waiting behind the global Redis semaphore for up to 300 seconds. Repeated clicks then created duplicate queued tasks for the same topic. A dedicated queue state is more truthful, prevents duplicate starts for the same card, and preserves the existing execution-timed rule that only the runner may advance to `briefing`.
alternatives: Keep returning 202 + optimistic `briefing` and rely on polling to snap back — rejected: this is exactly the misleading bounce the user reported
Advance durable topic runs to `briefing` in the HTTP request handler — rejected: it breaks the rule that execution stages must only flip at true execution points after semaphore claim
Expose no queue state at all and only disable the button locally — rejected: backend still needs duplicate-start protection and the user still needs truthful queue visibility
impact: Patched `api/routers/content_v13.py`, `core/models/pipeline_status.py`, `core/content_engine/state_redis.py`, and the Content Studio status/UI files to add `content_queued` end to end. Added regression coverage in `tests/api/test_content_v13_ga_endpoints.py`. Validation: `venv/bin/pytest tests/api/test_content_v13_ga_endpoints.py -q`, `venv/bin/pytest tests/content_engine/test_state_redis_ga.py -q`, and `cd frontend && npx tsc --noEmit`.

task: Operational cleanup boundary for resetting a company's Content Studio / TD-entry run history in local dev
decision: When a local test account needs a clean Content Studio slate, clear the company-scoped runtime-driving records rather than deleting `pipeline_runs` directly. The safe reset slice is: `content_engine_batch_runs`, `content_engine_topic_runs`, `content_engine_topic_events`, `content_pieces`, `content_artifacts`, company `api_tasks` for content-engine pipelines, the Redis hash `pipeline_state:{company_slug}`, and any leftover task SSE keys for the removed tasks. Do not treat `pipeline_runs` as a first-pass cleanup target unless the script also deletes the dependent GA analytics tables (`run_queries`, `run_citations`, `query_gaps`, embeddings tables, etc.) in the same transaction.
rationale: For the Webflow test account (`akeshri516@gmail.com`), the visible confusion in Content Studio came from stale runtime rows and Redis state, not from the deeper historical pipeline graph. A direct `pipeline_runs` delete failed immediately on `run_queries_run_id_fkey`, which confirmed that pipeline runs fan out into many analytics tables that are broader than the UI reset use case. Clearing the runtime-driving tables and Redis keys is enough to remove old cards, durable topic logs, and task records before a new TD-entry test pass while avoiding collateral damage to unrelated company data.
alternatives: Delete all company `pipeline_runs` for content-related pipeline types — rejected: unsafe without deleting a much larger dependency graph in the same transaction
Clear only Redis `pipeline_state:{slug}` and leave the database rows — rejected: old cards and task history would be able to repopulate from Postgres-backed endpoints
Delete the entire company row and recreate the account — rejected: far broader than the user-visible Content Studio reset that was requested
impact: For the Webflow test account, the cleanup zeroed `content_engine_batch_runs`, `content_engine_topic_runs`, `content_engine_topic_events`, `content_pieces`, `content_artifacts`, and content-engine `api_tasks`, and removed `pipeline_state:webflow` plus the remaining Webflow `sse:*` task-stream keys. `pipeline_runs` and its analytics dependents were intentionally left intact.

task: TD-entry GA card reconciliation — make poll responses authoritative after missed SSE transitions
decision: GA-phase topic-assignment cards must carry server-authored `created_at` and `updated_at` timestamps in Redis metadata and in the `/companies/{slug}/content/briefs` response. `write_ga_phase_state()` and `write_ga_phase_state_async()` now always upsert `__meta:ta-*` with timestamps, preserving the original `created_at` and bumping `updated_at` on every phase transition, even for status-only writes with no fresh topic_data payload. `DbContentDataService._load_ga_phase_cards()` now passes those timestamps through to `ContentBriefListItem` so frontend poll reconciliation can compare server recency against any locally stamped SSE state.
rationale: Live and poll paths were using different notions of recency. When a company SSE `state_changed` event updated a GA card locally, the frontend gave that card an `updatedAt`, but subsequent poll payloads for GA cards arrived with blank timestamps because the Redis-backed card serializer omitted them. The merge rule therefore kept stale local `gap_analysis` forever if the final `gap_analysis_complete` event was missed, leaving the card visually stuck in `Agent work` despite the backend having already persisted `gap_analysis_complete`. The fix belongs at the data source, not as a frontend-only exception, because any mixed live/poll path needs server timestamps to self-heal safely.
alternatives: Patch the frontend merge rule to special-case blank GA-card timestamps — rejected: hides the contract bug and keeps future live/poll flows fragile
Trust local SSE state over poll forever for GA cards — rejected: missed or dropped live events would remain unrecoverable
Move GA cards entirely off the `/content/briefs` poll path — deferred: poll reconciliation is still needed as a safety net even with authoritative live updates
impact: Patched `core/content_engine/state_redis.py` and `core/services/db_content_data.py`, added regression coverage in `tests/content_engine/test_state_redis_ga.py` and `tests/services/test_db_content_data_backend.py`, and documented the mixed live/poll lesson in memory. Validation: `venv/bin/pytest tests/content_engine/test_state_redis_ga.py -q` and `venv/bin/pytest tests/services/test_db_content_data_backend.py -k 'load_ga_phase_cards_includes_timestamps or passes_backend_not_path' -q`.

task: Company SSE Redis Streams transport — align XREAD heartbeats with Redis socket timeout
decision: The company-wide SSE stream must never block Redis longer than the configured socket timeout, and Redis read timeouts during an otherwise healthy idle stream should be treated as heartbeat ticks rather than fatal transport errors. `CompanyEventBus.stream()` now computes a safe `XREAD BLOCK` below `settings.redis_socket_timeout` and catches `redis.exceptions.TimeoutError` inside the live-tail loop to yield a heartbeat (`None`) instead of closing the SSE stream.
rationale: After migrating company SSE to Redis Streams, the company bus used `heartbeat_interval_s=30` directly as the Redis `XREAD BLOCK` value while the shared Redis client remained configured with `socket_timeout=20s`. Idle streams therefore timed out at the Redis socket layer first, producing repeated `Company event stream error ... closing SSE stream` log entries and forcing the frontend EventSource to reconnect even though nothing was actually wrong with the stream. The task SSE bus already avoided this class of issue by using a shorter block window, so the company bus needed the same transport discipline.
alternatives: Increase the global Redis socket timeout above 30s — rejected: broad infrastructure change for a single stream-loop bug
Keep the 30s block and simply suppress the exception log — rejected: the connection would still be torn down and reconnect unnecessarily
Disable Redis Streams heartbeats and rely entirely on browser reconnects — rejected: degrades live UX and hides the transport mismatch instead of fixing it
impact: Patched `core/events/company_event_bus.py` to cap `XREAD` block duration below the Redis socket timeout and to treat Redis read timeouts as idle heartbeats. Added regression coverage in `tests/events/test_company_event_bus.py`. Validation: `venv/bin/pytest tests/events/test_company_event_bus.py -q`.

task: TD-entry parallel execution — enrich durable topic events and lift the UI contract to generic card activity
decision: Keep TD-entry durable activity sourced from `content_engine_topic_events`, but enrich each returned event payload with stable run context on the service read path (`brief_id`, `display_id`, `topic_text`, `entry_mode`, `buyer_stage`, `intent_type`, `effective_slug`, `batch_run_id`) and attach explicit human-readable `note` payloads on runner completion/rollback transitions. On the frontend, stop binding the detail-view activity tab directly to `topic_run_*` naming; instead, use a generic card-activity adapter and `useCardActivity` hook that currently map TD topic-run events into reusable card-level activity items.
rationale: The TD topic log is now useful enough to become the base execution-log model, but the previous implementation still leaked TD-specific naming all the way into the UI and left too much interpretation to the frontend. Enriching the payload on read makes the append-only log more self-describing without requiring data backfills or new writes, and adding explicit notes on rollback/terminal transitions makes the user-visible timeline much clearer. Lifting the frontend boundary to a generic card-activity abstraction lets manual and future prompt-entry modes plug into the same tab and renderer later without forking a second logging experience before they have their own durable runtime source.
alternatives: Introduce a brand-new generic backend `card-runs` endpoint immediately — rejected: manual/prompt modes do not yet have a settled durable runtime identity, so a generic route now would mostly be a TD alias with extra churn
Keep the UI and hook named around `topic_run_*` until manual mode arrives — rejected: bakes TD-specific transport details into the component boundary we already know needs to be shared
Persist a second enriched event row format to the database — rejected: the stable run context already exists on the run row, so enriching on read is lower risk and applies to historical events too
impact: Added runner payload notes for GA/prod start, terminal completion/rejection, and production rollback; enriched service event snapshots with stable run context; introduced frontend `card-activity` adapter + `useCardActivity`; and rewired the Content Studio `Activity` tab to consume generic card-activity items while keeping TD backed by `topic_run_id`. Validation: `venv/bin/pytest tests/content_engine/test_topic_run_service.py -q`, `venv/bin/pytest tests/api/test_content_v13_ga_endpoints.py -q`, `venv/bin/pytest tests/api/test_content_v13_from_topics.py -k 'TestGetTopicRunEvents' -q`, and `npx tsc --noEmit`.

task: TD-entry parallel execution — expose the durable topic-level execution log in Content Studio
decision: The TD-entry card log is implemented as an additive read path over the existing durable `content_engine_topic_events` stream. The backend exposes `GET /api/v1/content/v13/{effective_slug}/topic-runs/{topic_run_id}/events`, scoped by the same exact company-boundary auth rules as `/topic-runs`, and the frontend loads that event list on demand inside the existing card detail view as a new `Activity` tab in the right sidebar. The log stays keyed by `topic_run_id` and preserves `display_id` as the visible identifier for the card.
rationale: The durable append-only event table already existed and was being populated by `topic_run_changed` and `topic_run_created`. Reusing that source avoids inventing a second execution-log channel or re-deriving history from coarse `state_changed` hints. Keeping the UI inside the existing card detail view makes the TD-first slice low-risk and immediately useful, while still matching the future direction of a generalized card-level log model for manual and prompt-entry modes.
alternatives: Build the topic log from company SSE replay instead of the durable event table — rejected: SSE is a transport, not the audit source of truth
Create a separate drawer/page for the log — rejected: unnecessary navigation churn; the existing card detail view is already the right execution context
Fetch activity by `display_id` alone — rejected: the durable runtime identity for TD-entry is `topic_run_id`, while `display_id` remains purely user-facing
impact: Added additive topic-event API schemas and route, a durable service read path over `content_engine_topic_events`, frontend API/types + `useTopicRunEvents`, and a new Content Studio `Activity` tab that renders the append-only event timeline for TD-entry cards. Validation: `venv/bin/pytest tests/api/test_content_v13_from_topics.py -q`, `venv/bin/pytest tests/api/test_content_v13.py -q`, and `npx tsc --noEmit`.

task: TD-entry parallel execution — harden durable/live-state correctness before topic-level logs
decision: TD-entry live state must be finalized per topic/card, not per batch. The topic-runs endpoint now enforces an exact company boundary (`company` or `company__product` only), production completion derives durable terminal states per `topic_assignment_id`, CE exception rollback mirrors the existing retryable `gap_analysis_complete` UX in durable topic runs, Stage 3 worker failures write an explicit durable `failed` transition immediately, and the frontend now treats run recency by `updated_at` while queuing debounced `state_changed` payloads instead of dropping earlier cards.
rationale: The review surfaced three ship-blocking backend regressions and two frontend reconciliation bugs. Prefix-based topic-run authorization leaked tenant data across similarly prefixed slugs. Batch-level durable completion writes clobbered mixed terminal outcomes, and CE crash handling persisted `failed` even when the visible card rolled back to a retryable queue state. Separately, Stage 3 worker failures could leave durable rows stuck at the last in-flight stage, cross-run recency could prefer an older historical run because `seq` is only per-run, and the reused debounce path dropped earlier `state_changed` payloads. Hardening these semantics is a prerequisite for exposing topic-level execution logs because the log must reflect the same authoritative card truth the UI renders.
alternatives: Proceed to topic-level logging first and clean up state correctness afterward — rejected: the log would amplify incorrect terminal state semantics
Keep batch-level terminal writes and let polling reconcile per-card truth — rejected: poll-only correction is exactly what the durable topic-run model is meant to replace

Preserve crash history by keeping durable live state at `failed` while the UI rolls back to queue state — rejected: authoritative live state must match the retryable UX; failure history belongs in events/payloads, not the current status field
impact: Patched router authorization, TD production finalization, rollback handling, Stage 3 worker failure propagation, and frontend topic-run reconciliation. Added regression coverage in `test_content_v13_from_topics.py`, `test_content_v13_ga_endpoints.py`, and `test_pipeline_v13.py`. Validation: `venv/bin/pytest tests/api/test_content_v13_from_topics.py -q`, `venv/bin/pytest tests/api/test_content_v13_ga_endpoints.py -q`, `venv/bin/pytest tests/content_engine/test_pipeline_v13.py -k 'td_worker_failure_writes_explicit_failed_state or TestRebriefContextExtraction or reject_with_rethink_triggers_rebrief or major_change_triggers_rebrief or max_rebriefs_then_rejected' -q`, and `npx tsc --noEmit`.

task: TD-entry parallel execution — finish remaining durable CE transition coverage
decision: TD-entry retry/rebrief/review/edit flows must preserve the original brief/display identity and must keep threading `session_factory` through every user-visible CE state write that depends on `_write_pipeline_state_async()`. In practice: TOPIC_DISCOVERY rebriefs reuse the existing `brief_id`/`display_id` instead of inventing a `rebrief-*` identity, and evaluator-driven `revising` plus rebrief worker/evaluator reruns now carry `session_factory` so the shared helper can keep appending durable topic-run events and emitting authoritative `topic_run_changed` payloads.
rationale: The audit found three remaining gaps after the first CE propagation slice. First, the TD HITL-2 `brief_review` write still omitted `session_factory`, so the frontend only got legacy `state_changed`. Second, evaluator revision loops wrote `revising` without durable context, so edit/retry paths depended on polling. Third, `_rebrief_and_rerun()` generated a new `rebrief-*` brief_id for TD-entry runs, which broke the durable brief_id lookup and undercut the universal display ID contract. Keeping the stable brief identity and durable context in these loops is required for authoritative live updates.
alternatives: Keep random `rebrief-*` IDs for TD-entry and rely on polling/state_changed to reconcile the UI — rejected: breaks durable brief_id matching and weakens the display_id contract
Patch the durable repo/service directly inside each retry branch — rejected: duplicates stage propagation logic instead of using the shared state-write helper

Scope the fix to only the initial HITL-2 branch and leave evaluator/rebrief loops coarse — rejected: users can see revising/rebrief/review transitions on the frontend, so those paths must be authoritative too
impact: Updated pipeline_v13 and evaluator loop call chains so TD `brief_review`, evaluator `revising`, and TD rebrief worker/evaluator reruns all preserve durable topic-run propagation. Added regression coverage in `test_td_hitl2.py`, `test_evaluator.py`, and `test_pipeline_v13.py`.

task: TD-entry parallel execution — frontend consumption of authoritative topic-run events
decision: Introduce a normalized Content Studio topic-run store keyed by topic_run_id with secondary indexes by topic_assignment_id and brief_id. `useCompanyStream` now consumes `topic_run_changed` directly and `useContentBriefs` overlays the durable topic-run snapshot onto polled cards, while `state_changed` is reduced to a compatibility patch path and polling remains only a reconciliation mechanism. The page-level company SSE subscription no longer refetches the board on every state change.
rationale: The previous frontend model treated company SSE as invalidation and depended on a refetch loop to discover the real state. That does not scale cleanly once multiple TD-entry runs are active in parallel and different cards can be in different CE stages simultaneously. The backend now emits durable, sequenced topic-run snapshots, so the frontend should consume them directly and only poll to self-heal missed events or non-TD state. A normalized store is required to handle out-of-order and duplicate updates safely.
alternatives: Keep refetch-on-state_changed and just add topic_run_changed for debugging — rejected: preserves coarse invalidation semantics and misses the main benefit of durable eventing
Store topic-run state directly on each card without normalization — rejected: duplicate/out-of-order events become harder to reason about and reconcile
Adopt a new global state library for this slice — rejected: unnecessary churn; a local normalized store plus pure merge/select helpers is enough
impact: Added frontend topic-run API types and fetcher, new pure topic-run store/overlay helpers, updated company stream hook contract, and rewired the board page to apply authoritative live deltas instead of immediate refetch. Validation: `npx tsc --noEmit` clean.

task: TD-entry parallel execution — fine-grained CE stage propagation and company-stream payloads
decision: Use the shared `_write_pipeline_state_async()` path as the source of truth for brief-level CE stage propagation. For TD-entry runs only, each brief-level state write now performs a best-effort durable topic-run update keyed by `(effective_slug, brief_id, pipeline_task_id)` and emits authoritative `topic_run_changed` company events with the durable row snapshot, while preserving the existing `state_changed` event for backward compatibility. A new brief-id scoped repository/service path was added instead of trying to infer topic runs from generic pipeline artifacts.
rationale: The shared state helper already sits on the hot path for `brief_review`, `pending_brief_approval`, worker stages like `drafting`/`linking`, evaluator transitions, and final completion/rejection states. Hooking durable propagation there keeps the CE runtime model aligned with the existing Redis/file state writes and avoids duplicating stage logic across many pipeline branches. Matching on task-scoped brief IDs is robust for TD-entry because `brief_id` is the display ID and the runner already rebinds the durable rows to the active production task before CE begins.
alternatives: Emit authoritative topic-run events only from worker dispatcher — rejected: misses other CE stages like approval/review/revising/rebrief transitions already funneled through `_write_pipeline_state_async`
Infer topic-run changes from generic `state_changed` events in the frontend — rejected: keeps backend state implicit and reintroduces ordering/glitch risk
Update topic runs by brief_id without task scoping — rejected: unsafe under retries or reused display IDs across future flows
impact: Added brief-id scoped durable update path in content_engine_run_repo/topic_run_service, threaded session_factory into CE state-write call sites, and expanded state_helpers tests to assert authoritative `topic_run_changed` emission alongside legacy `state_changed` compatibility events.

task: TD-entry parallel execution — harden durable topic-run identity and execution timing
decision: Durable topic-run writes must match a specific in-flight run, not 'latest row for this topic'. ContentEngineTopicRunService.advance_topic_runs now supports explicit match scopes: match_pipeline_task_id for the GA task that created the rows, and match_ga_run_id for production updates after GA completion. The previous unscoped fallback by topic_assignment_id was removed. The HTTP start-production route no longer advances durable rows to briefing; that transition now happens inside the runner after pipeline_semaphore acquisition, which is the first true execution point.
rationale: A topic_assignment_id can appear in multiple batches/retries. Updating by assignment alone can mutate the wrong historical run, especially once parallel TD-entry is enabled. GA completion is the moment the real ga_run_id becomes known, so that identifier must be bound back onto the exact rows originally created under the GA task. Separately, setting briefing in the request handler overstated progress while the job was still waiting for capacity, which would create frontend/backend drift under queueing pressure.
alternatives: Keep fallback-to-latest and rely on created_at ordering — rejected: incorrect under retries/overlapping batches
Advance to briefing in the request handler for snappier UI — rejected: misrepresents queued work as actively executing

Require topic_run_id from the frontend immediately for all mutations — deferred: additive API already returns it, but backend scoping fixes the immediate correctness issue without blocking current clients
impact: Repository query scoping widened (pipeline_task_id + effective_slug filters), durable service matching semantics tightened, production route optimistic state write removed, runner start path owns the briefing transition, and a regression DB test now covers reused topic_assignment_id across two GA tasks.

task: Layer 1 Constrained Decoding — add json_schema strict mode to 14 LLM call sites
decision: Create dedicated schema models (not reuse domain models) for OpenRouter constrained decoding. CE schemas in core/content_engine/structured_schemas.py (6 models), TD schemas in core/topic_discovery/structured_schemas.py (7 models). Shared build_response_format() helper in core/shared_tools/structured_output.py. All Dict[str, Any/T] fields replaced with typed sub-models (strict mode requires additionalProperties: false). Perplexity calls (Source C, Fact Enricher, Linker) and raw-markdown calls (Drafter, Formatter) excluded. require_parameters=True on all json_schema calls for routing safety.
rationale: Production crash on 2026-04-08: Brief Builder LLM returned content_format='technical_guide' instead of 5 allowed Literal values. Blind retries produced same invalid value. Zero blueprints. Pipeline failure. Constrained decoding prevents this class of error at the token level. Dedicated schema models chosen because: (1) domain models have post-parse fields (gap_context, id, embedding) that waste tokens and confuse the LLM, (2) Dict[str, Any] breaks strict mode, (3) clean contract for what LLM should output vs what system populates.
alternatives: Reuse domain models directly as response_format — rejected: Dict[str, Any] fields break strict mode, post-parse fields waste tokens
Use client.beta.chat.completions.parse() for auto-parsing — rejected: changes LLMResponse return type, breaks all 11+ existing callers
Use json_object mode (no schema enforcement) — rejected: does not prevent invalid Literal values, just ensures valid JSON
Use instructor library for validation-driven re-prompting — considered as Layer 2, orthogonal to Layer 1
impact: 6 new files + 10 modified files. 43 new tests. 14 LLM call sites wired. Token overhead: ~200-2000 tokens per request depending on schema complexity.
codex_review: gpt-5.3-codex critical review (473K tokens). 9 findings identified — see codex_findings below.

codex_findings.issue: Source B source_personas vs target_personas key mismatch — prompt uses source_personas, schema enforces target_personas, parser reads source_personas → persona_ids resolve to empty under constrained decoding
require_parameters sent at top level of extra_body; OpenRouter docs define it under provider.require_parameters (nested)
Hierarchy/unified S2 prompt uses pillar_name/pillar_description/subdomains; schema uses name/description/children — material key name mismatch
target_keywords prompt expects {primary, secondary[]}, schema enforces List[str]; UI/API expect object shape
reading_hierarchy prompt uses H1/H2/H3 (uppercase), schema uses h1/h2/h3 (lowercase); to_domain_model() normalizes but build_brief() parses to ContentBlueprint directly, bypassing schema model
No graceful downgrade if provider rejects json_schema — fails hard, no fallback to json_object mode
Non-trivial token overhead: CEContentBlueprintSchema ~2038 tokens, TDUnifiedHierarchySchema ~596 tokens
Several prompt example fields now forbidden by schema (user_feedback, rationale, example_topics) — wasted prompt instructions
Test suite passes but misses major prompt/schema contract regressions — need contract tests

task: Universal Display ID Part 2 — pipeline propagation + frontend + 6 audit fixes
decision: Part 2: Propagate display_id through orchestrator→Redis→CE→Content Data Service→Frontend. 6 audit fixes: H1 (brief_id_hint regex ^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9]{0,9}-\d{1,4}$), H2 (build_briefs_parallel preserves None entries for index alignment; all 7 callers filter after), M1 (JSON service regex), M2 (GA card dedup by topic_assignment_id in get_briefs), M3 (_brief_dir path sanitization), L1 (frontend fallback numbering from max existing).
rationale: H1: Content Studio 'Retry' button sends selectedCard.id (now WE-003) as brief_id_hint — old regex ^brief-\d{1,4}$ would 422-reject. H2: Pre-existing bug — build_briefs_parallel filtered None entries, collapsing indices. When topic 1 fails, topic 2's blueprint gets topic 1's assignment data. Now Nones preserved, callers map by index THEN filter. M2: If cleanup_ga_phase_state fails, both ta-{uuid} and WE-003 appear — dedup by topic_assignment_id prevents duplication. M3: Defense-in-depth — brief_id used as path segment, reject /, \, .., null. L1: Mixed backend/fallback display_ids could collide (both WE-001) — fallback now starts after max existing number.
alternatives: Remove brief_id_hint validation entirely — rejected: loses path traversal protection
Fix only TD caller for H2, leave others — rejected: all 7 callers could receive Nones
Full dedup by ta_id + brief_id hash — over-engineering: topic_assignment_id is sufficient
Sanitize at derive_prefix instead of _brief_dir — rejected: defense-in-depth at consumption point is safer
impact: 15 backend files + 7 frontend files modified, 3 new test files (37 tests). 240 affected tests passing. TypeScript clean.
codex_review: 2 rounds of gpt-5.3-codex review. Round 1: 6 findings (2 HIGH, 2 MEDIUM, 2 LOW) — all 6 fixed. Round 2: 3 new findings (2 HIGH-theoretical, 1 LOW) — deferred as low real-world risk. 106 tests run by Codex, all passing.
deferred_findings: Legacy pipeline.py _brief_dir has no sanitization (workers/dispatcher.py imports it) — LOW real risk, derive_prefix only produces [A-Z]
derive_prefix can produce digit-first prefix for digit-first company names (e.g. '3M' → '3M-001') which fails ^[A-Za-z] validator — extremely rare
build_briefs_parallel return type annotation says List[ContentBlueprint] but now includes None entries — type annotation drift

task: Fix Content Studio Kanban 4-minute sync lag — Codex audit recommendation R1
decision: Centralize _emit_company('state_changed') inside _write_pipeline_state_async() (after both Redis + file writes). Every status write automatically broadcasts a company SSE event. task: Refactor Pipeline B (topic expansion) to additive per-subdomain DB upserts
decision: Replace delete-all-reinsert-all pattern with per-subdomain atomic writes. task: Redis Session 5 — Distributed Semaphore Design Decisions
approach: Atomic Lua script for acquire (ZREMRANGEBYSCORE+ZCARD+ZADD in single call). Sorted Set with timestamp scores for self-healing. pipeline_semaphore(task_id) method (Option B from spec — explicit task_id, not context magic). 2h holder TTL without heartbeat. 1s polling interval without pub/sub wake-up.
rationale: Codex review confirmed P0 race condition in spec's non-atomic acquire — Lua script prevents two workers both seeing capacity and both ZADD. Option B is explicit (task_id at each call site) vs Option C's contextvars magic. 2h TTL acceptable: pipelines run minutes-to-hours, max 3 concurrent, heartbeat adds complexity for marginal benefit. 1s polling irrelevant vs pipeline duration (minutes).
alternatives_rejected: Non-atomic acquire (separate ZREMRANGEBYSCORE/ZCARD/ZADD) — race condition under contention
Short lease + heartbeat renew — over-engineering for max 3 pipelines running minutes-to-hours
Pub/Sub wake-up on release — adds failure modes (missed messages) for no practical gain
Fencing tokens — semaphore gates starts not shared mutable state, unnecessary
Option C (contextvars for task_id) — too magical, implicit coupling
outcome: 11 new tests, 14 runner call sites updated, 1 Codex P0 finding resolved, zero regressions. 9th Redis key in schema.

task: Redis Integration Sessions 0-2 — Architecture Decisions
approach: Dual Redis clients (async for hot paths, sync for locks/reads). Config toggles per feature (REDIS_EVENT_BUS, REDIS_PIPELINE_STATE). Graceful fallback to file/in-memory when Redis unavailable. Atomic Lua scripts for EventBus (INCR+XADD) and lock release (compare-and-delete). Fail-closed distributed locks when Redis is configured.
rationale: Async client prevents event loop blocking in pipeline hot paths (6-8 state writes per run). Sync client acceptable for sub-ms lock ops and to_thread readers. Config toggles allow incremental rollout. Lua scripts guarantee atomicity without multi-step race conditions. Fail-closed prevents split-brain in multi-worker.
alternatives_rejected: Sync Redis everywhere — would block event loop on state writes
Fail-open locks — split-brain risk in multi-worker deployment
Redis stream IDs for event sequencing — breaks Last-Event-ID int contract
Full hash DELETE on stale cleanup — clobbers parallel manual runs
No stale lock detection — accept false 409s until TTL
Per-process INCR counters — out-of-order writes across workers
outcome: 86 new tests, 8 Codex findings resolved, zero regressions. 4 Redis keys in schema.

task: SQLAlchemy + Alembic migration Phase 1 — ORM choice, schema design, repository pattern

Autogenerated first migration (known issues with pgvector extensions, enum creation, partial indexes)
Combined HNSW+schema migration (HNSW index creation locks tables in production)
Separate database_url_sync env var (drift risk — computed property from database_url eliminates it)
Repos owning commit() (breaks savepoint test isolation, prevents multi-repo atomicity)

Utility extraction enables middleware to operate without any service dependency. Protocol-based interface enables seamless swap from JSON to DB backend without touching any router code. Async-first design prepares for production DB usage.

Keep sync endpoints with sync DB calls (blocks on DB I/O, defeats async architecture)
Single AuthService class with conditional logic (violates SRP, harder to test)

Each has a JsonXxxService (wraps existing api/services/ functions via asyncio.to_thread) and a DbXxxService (uses SQL repos). task: TaskStore DB Migration — Protocol + DbTaskStore + lifespan DI switch
approach: TaskStoreProtocol (runtime_checkable Protocol) mirroring existing TaskStore API. Startup recovery loads non-terminal tasks, marks orphans as failed_restart. ApiTaskModel ORM with plain String status (not PG enum, because TaskStatus includes pending_approval/failed_restart). Lifespan _init_task_store() tries DbTaskStore when DATABASE_URL set, falls back to JSON TaskStore on failure. Session factory per-operation (not request-scoped).
rationale: Single-instance durability: task history persists across restarts, queryable task data. Protocol-based interface enables transparent swap. Write-through ensures DB durability for state transitions while keeping sync reads fast. Plain String status avoids PG enum limitations. Fallback to JSON ensures zero-downtime for existing deployments without DB.
alternatives_rejected: Write-behind (loses durability guarantees — Codex CX-13)
PG advisory locks for slug locks (over-engineering — in-memory locks sufficient for single instance)
PG enum for status column (missing pending_approval/failed_restart values — Codex CX-3)
Request-scoped sessions for DbTaskStore (long-lived singleton, not request lifecycle — Codex CX-4)
JSON→DB migration script (out of scope — DbTaskStore starts fresh, JSON preserved as-is — Codex CX-7)

task: Daily Tracker Integration — Orchestrator (Mediator), FastAPI router, DI wiring
approach: Mediator pattern orchestrator coordinates prompt library, platform runner, and mention detector — no direct module-to-module communication. Stateless orchestrator returns DailyRunResult (no DB dependency). API router provides 16 endpoints (8 prompt CRUD, 3 run management, 5 analytics) with auth/tenant isolation. Stateless orchestrator enables pure-mock testing (no DB setup needed). Orchestrator owns DB persistence (mixes orchestration with storage, harder to test)
Inline analytics computation in router (violates SRP, duplicates calculation logic)
Single monolithic DI function for all services (harder to override individually in tests)

task: Content Engine Pipeline v1.3 — two-phase context loading, LiteLLM, dual feedback loops, E-E-A-T
approach: 6-stage pipeline running alongside v1.0: (1) scorecard extraction (~11K tokens) for planner triage, (2) full context per-topic for Brief Builder, (3) workers accept ContentBlueprint (subclass of ContentBrief), (4) 5-dimension evaluator with dual feedback (section-level vs major-change), (5) 3 HITL checkpoints via LangGraph interrupt(). Workers modified in-place (swap SDK call → llm_call), shared between both pipelines. _ensure_litellm_model() auto-prefixes model strings for backward compat.
rationale: Full gap analysis output (80-120K tokens) created context explosion for the v1.0 planner. Two-phase loading reduces planner context to ~11K tokens. ContentBlueprint extends ContentBrief so all existing workers accept it transparently (zero type hint changes). LiteLLM provides model abstraction for benchmarking + easy provider switches. Dual feedback loops prevent expensive re-briefs from automated evaluator false positives — major direction change only from HITL-3 human rejection or semantic score < 0.5. E-E-A-T adds content quality signal missing from v1.0's 4-dimension evaluation.
alternatives_rejected: Separate v1.3 worker copies (90% code duplication, maintenance nightmare)
Replace v1.0 pipeline entirely (breaks existing content runs, no fallback)
LangChain for LLM abstraction (inconsistent with gap analysis, hides control)
Runtime prompt pulls from LangSmith Hub (adds availability dependency — prompts stay in Python files)
Major direction change from automated evaluator (too expensive, false positive risk)
outcome: Phases A-D1-D2 complete. 14 new files created, 9 files modified. 211 content+research tests passing. v1.0 pipeline fully preserved. Workers shared between both pipelines via LiteLLM.

task: Question-heading classification without trailing ?

task: Universal Display ID System — backend-generated per-company IDs (WE-001, IH-042) for topic assignments
decision: Per-company counter on companies table (display_id_prefix + display_id_counter) with SELECT FOR UPDATE for atomicity. backfill_display_ids() called after every bulk write. Gap-tolerant (Linear-style). display_id stored on topic_assignments. Carried through Pydantic model during delete+insert cycles. AUTONOMOUS/MANUAL CE modes keep brief-NNN fallback.

Codex reviewed plan: PASS — no CRITICAL/HIGH/MEDIUM findings.

Reuse deleted IDs — rejected: confusing for users, complex logic
Generate display_ids for AUTONOMOUS/MANUAL modes — deferred: no TopicAssignment exists

task: Codex kickoff for TD-entry parallel execution architecture
decision: Introduce durable content_engine_batch_runs + content_engine_topic_runs + content_engine_topic_events as the new execution spine for TD-entry Content Engine. Every topic-run row carries both topic_assignment_id and display_id, with display_id also copied into the event log. TD gap-analysis task creation now uses allow_parallel=True so company-level slug exclusivity no longer blocks parallel TD-entry batches. The global semaphore still caps overall pipeline concurrency.
rationale: The existing system already had topic_assignment_id at the data layer and display_id as the human-facing identifier, but runtime execution was still primarily task-centric and partially lock-centric. The new requirement needs per-topic durability, parallel multi-batch execution, and a user-visible identity that remains display_id-first. Removing only the old lock without introducing durable topic-run records would make the frontend harder to reconcile and would not give us auditability.
alternatives: Keep company-level slug lock and only allow parallelism inside a single batch — rejected because the user explicitly needs multiple batches in parallel
Use topic_assignment_id only and derive display_id at render time — rejected because display_id is the conversation and Kanban identity
Continue relying on file-backed pipeline state for the new flow — rejected because multi-worker consistency and replay become fragile
outcome: Foundation slice implemented on branch codex-td-entry-parallelism-plan. TD GA start now creates durable batch/topic-run rows best-effort and returns additive batch_run_id/topic_runs fields. Added GET /api/v1/content/v13/{effective_slug}/topic-runs. Coarse topic-run status advancement wired on GA/prod start and runner terminal paths. Targeted validation: 52 passed, 2 skipped.

task: Replace process-local company event streaming with Redis Streams
decision: Move CompanyEventBus from process-local queue fanout to Redis Streams-backed delivery in production, while preserving the same synchronous emit(company_slug, CompanyEvent(...)) publisher API. The /api/v1/companies/{company_slug}/stream SSE endpoint now reads sequenced company events from Redis Streams, includes SSE id values, and honors Last-Event-ID for replay. A small in-memory path remains only when CompanyEventBus is instantiated without Redis in tests.
rationale: The Kanban and Content Studio rely on company-scoped state invalidation and notification events. In the old implementation those events only reached subscribers connected to the same worker process, which breaks in multi-worker deployment. Redis Streams aligns the company stream with the existing task SSE architecture and gives replay semantics needed for reconnect correctness.
alternatives: Keep the in-memory company bus and rely on sticky sessions — rejected because it is not robust enough for enterprise multi-worker deployment
Use Redis Pub/Sub only — rejected because replay on reconnect is materially weaker
Move immediately to topic_run_changed-only events before transport replacement — rejected because transport correctness is the prerequisite
outcome: Company event transport now uses Redis Streams in production. Startup config wires the singleton with app.state.redis and the running loop. SSE responses now carry id fields and support Last-Event-ID replay. Targeted validation: 80 passed.

task: Phase 2 concurrency split for Content Engine parallelism
decision: Content Engine concurrency is now isolated from the shared singleton-pipeline pool and capped per company, not globally across all tenants. `DbTaskStore` keeps the existing shared Redis semaphore `semaphore:pipelines` for singleton workloads, but CE pipelines (`content`, `content_v13`, and `td_content`, including TD start-production) now acquire a separate semaphore named `semaphore:content_engine:{company_slug}` with default capacity 15. HITL heartbeat renewal and startup orphan cleanup route to the correct semaphore family based on the persisted task pipeline.
rationale: The prior global semaphore let one tenant's CE traffic block unrelated companies and unrelated singleton pipelines. The user clarified that CE apparent parallelism should scale per tenant while company-scoped singleton pipelines remain exclusive. Splitting the pools is the smallest safe Phase 2 change that removes cross-company CE interference without yet redesigning CE scheduling around topic-run claims.
alternatives: Raise the shared global semaphore limit for everyone — rejected because it still lets one company starve another and mixes CE with singleton workloads
Move directly to the full topic-run dispatcher before splitting pools — rejected for this step because it is a larger Phase 3 scheduler change and would delay the immediate per-tenant throughput fix
Key CE semaphores by effective_slug/product — rejected because the requirement is tenant/company capacity, not per-product isolation
outcome: Phase 2 implemented. CE runners now request the company-scoped pool, while singleton pipelines remain on the shared pool. Validation: `venv/bin/pytest tests/services/test_redis_semaphore.py tests/services/test_heartbeat_renewal.py -q` (31 passed) and `venv/bin/pytest tests/services/test_db_task_store.py tests/api/test_content.py tests/api/test_gap_runner.py tests/api/test_content_v13_ga_endpoints.py -q` (94 passed, pre-existing warnings). Phase 3 still needs the durable topic-run dispatcher, topic-level active claims, and slot release/reclaim around HITL waits.

task: Phase 3 TD-entry scheduler — durable per-topic queue plus dispatcher
decision: TD `start-production` no longer maps one request to one long-lived CE task. The route now queues the existing durable `content_engine_topic_runs` rows by setting them to `content_queued` with persisted `launch_context`, then immediately asks a dispatcher to claim queued rows up to the company CE capacity. Claims are company-wide and durable: `ContentEngineTopicRunRepository.claim_queued_runs_for_company()` uses `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` over `content_queued` rows whose `metadata_json.dispatch_state` is `queued` or unset. Each claimed topic run gets its own `td_content` task and pipeline_task_id, so TD production is now task-per-topic rather than task-per-click. Response payloads return additive `topic_runs` snapshots, and the frontend now reads the per-topic `pipeline_task_id` from those snapshots instead of trusting a single route-level `run_id`.
rationale: The Phase 2 per-company CE semaphore fixed cross-tenant interference but still left the product in a runner-per-click model. That model makes overflow work sit behind semaphores as invisible waiting tasks and does not express the durable queue at the topic/card level. The durable topic-run table already exists and is the right queue primitive for TD-entry. Using it as the dispatch source is the smallest Phase 3 step that introduces real topic/card queue semantics without yet tackling Phase 4 slot release around HITL.
alternatives: Keep spawning one CE task per request and let extra tasks wait behind the semaphore — rejected because it still hides the queue in task runtime rather than durable card state
Jump straight to Phase 4 slot release/reclaim around HITL — rejected for this slice because Phase 3 first needs durable per-topic dispatch and one-task-per-topic execution units
Add brand-new scheduler tables — rejected because `content_engine_topic_runs` already carries the durable per-card identity and state we need
outcome: Phase 3 slice implemented. Start-production now queues topic runs durably, dispatches claimed rows up to available company CE capacity, and launches one `td_content` task per claimed topic. Runner completion triggers another dispatch pass so queued topics drain automatically as slots free up. Validation: `venv/bin/pytest tests/api/test_content_v13_ga_endpoints.py -q` (28 passed, 2 pre-existing warnings), `venv/bin/pytest tests/content_engine/test_topic_run_service.py tests/services/test_redis_semaphore.py tests/services/test_heartbeat_renewal.py tests/api/test_content_v13_ga_endpoints.py -q` (61 passed, 2 pre-existing warnings), and `cd frontend && npx tsc --noEmit` (clean). Phase 4 still needs slot release/reclaim around HITL waits and stronger claim-state persistence than JSON metadata.

task: Phase 4 CE throughput fix — release company CE slots during HITL waits
decision: CE tasks should not consume a company execution slot while they are blocked on human approval. `DbTaskStore.wait_for_approval()` now detects active CE tasks, suspends the active semaphore context before waiting, and reacquires that same company-scoped slot before handing the approval payload back to the graph. The tracked semaphore context supports suspend/resume for both Redis-backed and local asyncio fallback semaphores. While suspended, `_renew_leases()` skips semaphore renewal, and the TD dispatcher excludes `TaskStatus.PENDING_APPROVAL` CE tasks from `_count_active_company_ce_tasks()` so waiting-human cards do not count against the per-company runnable cap.
rationale: Phase 3 introduced a durable topic-run queue and per-topic dispatcher, but CE slots were still held for the entire task lifetime because the semaphore wrapped the full runner and the approval wait loop kept renewing that lease. That meant a card sitting in `pending_brief_approval` or `pending_content_approval` still blocked queued topics from starting, which defeats the product goal of 15+ apparent parallel cards per company. Releasing the slot during HITL keeps the existing task/graph contract intact while materially increasing runnable throughput.
alternatives: Keep renewing the semaphore during HITL and only raise the company cap — rejected because human waits would still waste capacity and the system would scale poorly at 15-30 topics

Move immediately to dedicated scheduler columns plus full continuation jobs for approval resumes — deferred to a later phase because the tracked-context suspend/resume change is smaller and safe on the current architecture
Exclude `PENDING_APPROVAL` from the dispatcher count without actually releasing the semaphore — rejected because queued tasks would still fail to acquire the underlying slot
outcome: Phase 4 slice implemented. CE approval waits now suspend/reacquire the active company semaphore slot, and queued TD topic runs can keep dispatching while another card is waiting on human input. Validation: `venv/bin/pytest tests/services/test_redis_semaphore.py tests/services/test_heartbeat_renewal.py tests/services/test_db_task_store.py tests/services/test_approval_queue_redis.py tests/api/test_content_v13_ga_endpoints.py -q` (115 passed, pre-existing warnings) and `venv/bin/python -m compileall core/services/db_task_store.py core/redis_semaphore.py api/tasks/runner.py`.

task: Phase 5 TD-entry scheduler hardening — dedicated scheduler columns and durable approval continuations
decision: TD scheduler state now belongs in first-class `content_engine_topic_runs` columns rather than `metadata_json`. Migration 0039 adds `scheduler_state`, `claim_token`, `queued_at`, `claimed_at`, `waiting_for_human_at`, and `continuation_payload_json`, and the repository/service claim path now uses those columns directly. TD HITL-2 and HITL-3 checkpoints no longer wait for approval inside the same worker task: `run_hitl_checkpoint(... external_resume=True)` raises `ApprovalPauseRequested` with a persisted continuation payload, the runner records the topic run as `waiting_human`, and the approval routes record the user decision with `delivery_mode='record_only'`, mark the topic run `resume_queued`, and immediately redispatch it. Resume claims reuse the same `td_content` task id and feed the stored LangGraph `thread_id` plus approval payload back into the graph so continuation picks up from the durable checkpoint instead of forking a new task identity.
rationale: Phase 3 and 4 introduced per-topic dispatch plus slot release around HITL, but the scheduler still hid claim state inside JSON metadata and approvals still resumed inside the same long-lived task. That left the system brittle at approval boundaries and made the durable topic-run layer observational instead of authoritative. Moving scheduler state to dedicated columns and turning approvals into explicit queued continuations makes the TD runtime model align with the durable topic-run identity we want to generalize later for manual/prompt entry.
alternatives: Keep `metadata_json.dispatch_state` as the scheduler source of truth and only add more helper methods around it — rejected because queue/claim/wait state is now a primary runtime concern, not incidental metadata

Continue resuming TD approvals inside the same task after Phase 4 semaphore suspend/reacquire — rejected because it still ties approval progression to one long-lived worker and blocks a clean durable scheduler model
Create a second continuation table for TD resumes — rejected because the topic-run row already owns the card identity and should remain the single durable scheduler record
outcome: Phase 5 implemented for TD-entry. Topic-run scheduler state is now column-backed, TD brief/content approvals become durable queued continuations, and dispatcher resume claims reuse the existing task id while resuming the LangGraph checkpoint from stored continuation payload. Also corrected a Phase 2 regression so singleton runners like `gap_analysis` and `site_audit` remain on the shared pool instead of the CE company pool. Validation: `venv/bin/pytest tests/api/test_content_v13.py tests/api/test_content_v13_ga_endpoints.py tests/content_engine/test_graph_v13.py tests/services/test_approval_queue_redis.py -q` (179 passed, pre-existing warnings) and `venv/bin/pytest tests/content_engine/test_pipeline_v13.py -k 'test_td_worker_failure_writes_explicit_failed_state or test_td_rebrief_preserves_brief_id_and_threads_session_factory' -q` (2 passed, 1 pre-existing AsyncMock warning).

task: Phase 5 follow-up hardening — make TD durable scheduler transitions the commit point for approvals and start-production
decision: TD approval routes must validate nonce/window first, then durably transition the matching topic run from `waiting_human` to `resume_queued`, and only after that record approval history on the task. TD routes no longer rely on `submit_approval(... delivery_mode='record_only')` because the Redis approval flag is not the correct duplicate guard for durable continuations. Duplicate or late TD approvals are now rejected by the durable scheduler state itself: `queue_topic_run_resume()` only succeeds for runs currently in `waiting_human`. Similarly, TD start-production must fail closed unless `queue_topic_runs_for_dispatch()` actually queued at least one durable topic run; mirroring `content_queued` to GA Redis now happens only after durable queue success. Scheduler update APIs now use explicit tri-state field semantics so requeueing can clear stale nullable runtime fields such as `pipeline_task_id`, `claimed_at`, and `waiting_for_human_at`.
rationale: The initial Phase 5 continuation implementation left the durable scheduler as a best-effort sidecar after task-store mutation. That created three review regressions: approvals could become permanently un-retryable if the durable queue step failed after `approval:flag:{task_id}` was set, start-production could still return 202 when no durable work was queued, and queued retries could leak stale task ids back to the frontend because `None` meant 'leave unchanged' rather than 'clear'. Once `content_engine_topic_runs` owns scheduling, router truthfulness must be anchored to the durable scheduler transition itself.
alternatives: Keep using `submit_approval(... record_only)` for TD and try to clear Redis approval flags on downstream failures — rejected because it still treats the task-store flag as primary instead of the durable scheduler state
Continue returning 202 after any queue/dispatch exception and rely on later dispatcher passes — rejected because the route would still be lying when no durable queue exists at all
Use booleans like `clear_pipeline_task_id=True` for every nullable scheduler field — rejected in favor of a generic tri-state update contract that can be reused for other scheduler fields
outcome: Follow-up hardening implemented. TD approvals now queue the durable continuation before recording approval history, start-production returns failure if no durable queue was created, and requeueing clears stale task ids/claim timestamps before serializing queued topic runs back to the frontend. Validation: `venv/bin/pytest tests/api/test_content_v13.py tests/api/test_content_v13_ga_endpoints.py tests/content_engine/test_topic_run_service.py tests/services/test_approval_queue_redis.py -q` (131 passed, pre-existing warnings), `venv/bin/pytest tests/services/test_db_task_store.py tests/api/test_content_v13.py tests/api/test_content_v13_ga_endpoints.py tests/content_engine/test_topic_run_service.py tests/services/test_approval_queue_redis.py -q` (166 passed, pre-existing warnings), and `venv/bin/python -m py_compile api/routers/content_v13.py core/services/db_task_store.py core/services/task_store.py core/services/content_engine_topic_runs.py tests/api/test_content_v13.py tests/api/test_content_v13_ga_endpoints.py tests/content_engine/test_topic_run_service.py`.

task: Phase 6 TD-entry scheduler hardening — startup reconciliation and auto-dispatch after restart
decision: `content_engine_topic_runs` is now the startup recovery source of truth for TD-entry. On FastAPI boot, the app gathers recovered task rows from `DbTaskStore`, runs a scheduler reconciliation pass over topic runs in `queued`, `resume_queued`, `claimed`, `running`, and `waiting_human`, then auto-dispatches each company that still has recoverable queued work. Recovery rules are state-aware: `waiting_human` stays intact; `queued` / `resume_queued` clear stale `pipeline_task_id` values if the referenced task no longer exists; `claimed` / `running` with a failed/missing/cancelled task and a continuation payload are repaired to `resume_queued`; `claimed` / `running` with a failed-restart task carrying approval checkpoint data are restored to `waiting_human`; and plain stranded `claimed` / `running` rows without a continuation are requeued back to `content_queued`.
rationale: By the end of Phase 5, normal TD approval/resume flow was durable, but restart behavior was still incomplete. A process death between durable queueing and dispatch, or during `claimed` / `running`, could leave topic runs stranded until some later user action happened to trigger dispatch again. The task store already marks orphaned tasks `failed_restart`, but task recovery and topic-run recovery were still separate systems. Phase 6 closes that gap by reconciling durable topic-run scheduler state against recovered task state at boot and treating the topic run, not the task row, as the durable runtime authority.
alternatives: Rely only on task-store startup recovery and wait for users to retrigger dispatch manually — rejected because queued/resume-queued cards could remain stranded indefinitely after restart
Treat every non-terminal `claimed` / `running` row as immediately requeueable on startup — rejected because a second worker/process may still legitimately own a live running task
Add a separate recovery queue/table for paused TD approvals — rejected because the topic-run row already owns the durable scheduler identity and continuation payload
outcome: Phase 6 implemented. Startup now repairs stranded TD scheduler rows, restores failed-restart approval checkpoints back to `waiting_human`, requeues stranded continuations as `resume_queued`, requeues plain stranded runs as `content_queued`, clears stale task ids on queued work, and immediately auto-dispatches companies with recovered queueable work. Validation: `venv/bin/pytest tests/content_engine/test_topic_run_service.py tests/api/test_lifespan_task_store.py -q` (10 passed), `venv/bin/pytest tests/content_engine/test_topic_run_service.py tests/api/test_lifespan_task_store.py tests/api/test_content_v13_ga_endpoints.py -q` (44 passed, 2 pre-existing warnings), and `venv/bin/pytest tests/api/test_lifespan_task_store.py tests/services/test_db_task_store.py tests/services/test_approval_queue_redis.py tests/api/test_content_v13.py tests/api/test_content_v13_ga_endpoints.py tests/content_engine/test_topic_run_service.py -q` (174 passed, 35 pre-existing warnings).

task: Content Studio agent-stage visibility and final-review loading resilience during TD QA
decision: The Content Studio board should always render visible agent-stage text from the authoritative card status, even when per-task `agentProgress` metadata is missing. `agentProgress` is now treated as an optional enhancement for percentages and progress bars rather than the prerequisite for showing `Briefing`, `Outlining`, `Drafting`, and similar stage labels. Review/pending-content-approval detail views must also render a non-blank fallback shell whenever article content is still loading or the stage-content fetch failed. On the backend, `DbContentDataService.get_briefs()` should not query `PipelineRepository.get_latest_completed()` in the common case where slug-scoped `content_pieces` already exist, and the default async DB pool was raised from `5/10` to `15/20` to better match concurrent local QA polling.
rationale: Manual QA showed that the backend and company stream were already emitting correct stage transitions, but the board hid them whenever `agentProgress` was absent because that metadata only comes from the per-task SSE path. The same session showed blank final-review detail panes even though the backend brief/enriched endpoints returned 200s; the frontend was failing soft to `articleContent = null` and then rendering nothing. Backend pool-exhaustion logs showed that repeated `/content/briefs` polling was also paying for an avoidable latest-run lookup on every poll, worsening the perceived delay.
alternatives: Keep stage text coupled to `agentProgress` and rely on per-task SSE to always be present — rejected because the company-stream/status path already carries enough information to label the card
Keep swallowing stage-content fetch failures and accept a blank review pane — rejected because users need a visible loading/error state during HITL-3
Only raise the DB pool size without reducing hot-path work — rejected because the avoidable `get_latest_completed()` query would still scale poorly with poll traffic
outcome: Implemented on 2026-04-10. Active agent cards now show a visible stage label even without `agentProgress`, review-stage detail views render a fallback instead of a blank pane when final content is unavailable, metrics math no longer emits `NaN` for empty arrays/zero targets, `/content/briefs` skips the latest-run lookup when slug-scoped pieces exist, and the default DB pool is larger for concurrent QA traffic. Validation: `venv/bin/pytest tests/services/test_db_content_data_backend.py -q` (9 passed), `cd frontend && npx tsc --noEmit` (clean), and `venv/bin/python -m py_compile core/services/db_content_data.py core/config/settings.py`.

task: Topic-scoped TD gap-analysis detail view for Queue-column cards
decision: Queue/detail GA views for TD `ta-*` cards must use a topic-specific summarized `gap_context` carried on the GA card payload itself, not a batch-level `ga_run_id` summary lookup. The authoritative contract is now: at TD GA completion, the orchestrator loads the topic-scoped `analysis.json` artifact, derives one `GapContextSummary`-shaped payload per assignment from `extract_topic_contexts(...)`, writes that summary into the GA card Redis metadata, and `/content/briefs` passes it through to `ContentBriefListItem.gap_context` for the frontend detail view.
rationale: Manual QA showed that after the frontend stopped using the batch-level summary for Queue/detail cards, topic-scoped GA cards still rendered blank metrics (`Gap Score —`, `Classification —`) because the backend never supplied topic-level `gap_context` on `ta-*` cards. Reusing the CE pipeline's topic-context extraction keeps the topic-scoped semantics correct, while serializing only the summarized `GapContextSummary` avoids leaking the full internal worker-context shape into the frontend contract.
alternatives: Keep using `/gap-analysis/summary?ga_run_id=...` in the detail view — rejected because TD topic-scoped GA runs are batch-scoped and a single card should not display aggregated metrics for the whole batch

Serialize the full `WorkerQueryContext` into the card payload and let the frontend derive a summary — rejected because it would widen the frontend/backend contract unnecessarily and expose internal CE data structures
Leave topic-level metrics to a second on-demand detail endpoint — rejected because the Queue-column card already has a durable GA card identity and should be self-contained in `/content/briefs`
outcome: Implemented on 2026-04-10. TD GA-complete writes now attach one summarized topic-level `gap_context` per assignment, the Redis GA card read path preserves that payload, and `DbContentDataService._load_ga_phase_cards()` exposes it on `ContentBriefListItem.gap_context` so Queue/detail views can render topic-scoped metrics immediately after Phase 1. Validation: `venv/bin/pytest tests/content_engine/test_state_redis_ga.py tests/services/test_db_content_data_backend.py -q` (29 passed), `venv/bin/pytest tests/orchestration/test_td_ga_only.py -k gap_analysis_complete_write_includes_topic_gap_context -q` (1 passed), and `venv/bin/python -m py_compile core/orchestration/td_content_orchestrator.py core/content_engine/state_redis.py core/services/db_content_data.py` (clean).

task: Content Studio active TD-entry detail view sidebar content
decision: For TD-entry cards that originated from Topic Discovery, the left sidebar in active CE and brief-approval detail views should preserve the Topic Discovery assignment context instead of showing only runtime pipeline telemetry. The planner-derived topic metadata block (topic description, buyer stage, intent, content spec, target keywords, topic angle, priority factors, and persona context) is now reused across GA, active CE, and brief-approval views. Final article-review views still keep the article section navigator because section jumping is more valuable there.
rationale: Manual QA showed that once a TD card left Queue and entered active brief-building or later CE stages, the left sidebar lost the original planner assignment context even though that context is still what the user needs to judge whether the pipeline is on the right topic. The center panel already displays pipeline progress for active CE work, so the sidebar should carry forward the Topic Discovery framing rather than duplicating runtime telemetry.
alternatives: Keep the old agent-only sidebar everywhere after Queue — rejected because it hides the original topic assignment context during the most important human supervision stages
Replace the sidebar even for final article review — rejected because section navigation remains the higher-value affordance while reviewing final article text
Create a second independent topic-context sidebar implementation for active CE views — rejected because the GA sidebar already defined the right contract and could be reused directly
outcome: Implemented on 2026-04-11. Active TD-entry detail views and brief-approval views now render the same topic-assignment metadata block that Queue/GA views use, while final review continues to use the article section navigator. Validation: `cd frontend && npx tsc --noEmit`.

task: Content Studio active TD-entry detail view right-sidebar metrics
decision: Active TD-entry CE and approval views should keep rendering the same topic-specific gap-analysis metrics as Queue-column cards by sourcing `gap_context` from the persisted `content_pieces.evaluation_results` payload. Blueprint persistence now stores topic-level `gap_context` early, CE piece upserts preserve an existing `evaluation_results.gap_context` when later eval summaries do not include it, and `DbContentDataService.get_briefs()` passes any embedded `evaluation_results.gap_context` through `extract_gap_context()` before falling back to analysis-file lookups.
rationale: The frontend Metrics sidebar already renders `GapAnalysisSection` whenever `card.gapContext` exists, so the blank metrics in active CE views were a backend contract problem, not a UI rendering gap. TD GA queue cards carried topic-specific `gap_context` through Redis, but once a topic moved into `content_pieces`, later persistence writes could erase that field and the DB-backed brief read path ignored any embedded gap context. Preserving `gap_context` at the DB piece layer keeps Queue, active CE, and approval views aligned on the same topic-scoped GA data without requiring another frontend-only special case.
alternatives: Fetch batch-level gap-analysis summary again in active CE views — rejected because the user needs metrics for the specific topic assignment, not the whole TD GA batch
Teach the frontend to retain the old Queue-card `gapContext` in local state forever — rejected because reloading/polling would still lose the data and the backend contract would remain inconsistent
Persist the full internal worker context in a separate table just for sidebar metrics — rejected because `evaluation_results.gap_context` already provides the right durable hook with less churn
outcome: Implemented on 2026-04-11. Topic-level `gap_context` now survives the transition from Redis GA cards into DB-backed `content_pieces`, and active CE right-sidebar Metrics views keep showing the same topic-specific GA metrics that Queue/detail views show.
